name: architecture-patterns
description: Choose and apply architectural patterns (layered, hexagonal, microservices, monolith, event-driven) for the real constraints. Use when structuring a system.
checklist: Simplest thing that could work chosen

name: design-patterns
description: Apply classic design patterns (factory, strategy, observer, adapter, etc.) where they simplify, not where they add ceremony. Use when structuring code.
checklist: Pattern reduces complexity, not adds it
Language idioms preferred over forced patterns
pitfalls: Forcing GoF patterns onto simple problems

name: clean-architecture
description: Apply clean/onion architecture: dependency inversion, domain independence from frameworks, testable boundaries. Use when isolating business logic.
pitfalls: Framework types leaking into the domain
Anemic domain with logic in services

name: domain-driven-design
description: Apply DDD: ubiquitous language, bounded contexts, aggregates, entities/value objects. Use for complex business domains.
checklist: Ubiquitous language shared with domain experts
pitfalls: DDD ceremony on a CRUD app

name: event-driven-architecture
description: Design event-driven systems: events, pub/sub, choreography vs orchestration, eventual consistency. Use for decoupled/async systems.

name: hexagonal-architecture
description: Apply ports-and-adapters (hexagonal) architecture: core logic behind ports, adapters for IO. Use to isolate and test core logic.
checklist: Core depends on ports, not adapters

name: cqrs-event-sourcing
description: Apply CQRS and event sourcing where justified: separate read/write models, event log as source of truth. Use for audit-heavy/complex-write domains.

name: api-design
description: Design clear, consistent, evolvable APIs (REST/GraphQL/RPC): naming, versioning, errors, pagination, backward compatibility. Use when designing any API.
pitfalls: Leaking internal models as the contract

name: system-design
description: Design systems at scale: requirements, capacity, data flow, storage, caching, tradeoffs, failure modes. Use for high-level design tasks/interviews.
pitfalls: Designing for scale you'll never hit

name: scalability-patterns
description: Scale systems: horizontal scaling, sharding, replication, caching, async, statelessness, back-pressure. Use when a system must handle more load.
checklist: Caching and async offload hot paths

name: distributed-systems
description: Reason about distributed systems: CAP, consistency models, consensus, partial failure, idempotency, clocks. Use for multi-node systems.

name: idempotency-patterns
description: Make operations idempotent: idempotency keys, dedup, upserts, exactly-once semantics. Use for retryable/async operations and payments.

name: twelve-factor-app
description: Apply the twelve-factor methodology: config in env, stateless processes, logs as streams, dev/prod parity. Use for cloud-native apps.
checklist: Logs to stdout as event streams

name: concurrency-patterns
description: Write correct concurrent code: threads, async, locks, channels, immutability, avoiding races/deadlocks. Use for multithreaded/async code.

name: memory-management
description: Manage memory correctly: allocation, ownership, leaks, GC tuning, fragmentation across languages. Use for memory bugs/leaks/tuning.
checklist: GC pressure minimized in hot paths

name: algorithms-data-structures
description: Choose the right algorithm/data structure and reason about complexity (Big-O), tradeoffs, and correctness. Use for algorithmic problems.

name: oop-principles
description: Apply OOP/SOLID sensibly: encapsulation, composition over inheritance, single responsibility, dependency inversion. Use when designing OO code.

name: functional-programming
description: Apply functional techniques: pure functions, immutability, composition, higher-order functions, effects at edges. Use to reduce state bugs.
checklist: Pure core; side effects at the edges

name: error-handling
description: Handle errors robustly: fail loud, propagate context, no silent swallowing, typed errors, retries where safe. Use whenever code can fail.

name: silent-failure-detection
description: Find and fix silent failures: swallowed errors, bad fallbacks, missing propagation, ignored return codes. Use when reviewing for hidden failures.
pitfalls: Default values masking a failed call

name: logging-best-practices
description: Log usefully: levels, structure, correlation ids, no secrets/PII, actionable messages. Use when adding logging.

name: code-comments
description: Write comments that explain why, not what; keep them accurate; avoid comment rot. Use when documenting non-obvious code.

name: technical-debt-management
description: Identify, track and pay down technical debt deliberately: inventory, prioritization, incremental refactor, boy-scout rule. Use when managing debt.
pitfalls: Refactoring with no test safety net

name: architecture-decision-records
description: Capture architectural decisions as ADRs: context, decision, consequences, status. Use when making significant technical decisions.
pitfalls: Decisions living only in people's heads

name: requirements-analysis
description: Clarify requirements before building: user needs, acceptance criteria, edge cases, non-functional needs, ambiguity. Use before implementation.
pitfalls: Building the wrong thing from vague specs

name: tech-writing
description: Write clear technical content: structure for the reader, concrete examples, no jargon dumps, task-oriented. Use for docs, RFCs, guides, PRs.

name: estimation-planning
description: Estimate and plan work realistically: decomposition, uncertainty, ranges not points, buffers, scope negotiation. Use when planning tasks.

name: tdd-workflow
description: Practice test-driven development: red-green-refactor, small steps, test-first, behavior focus. Use when TDD is desired.

name: bdd-testing
description: Practice behavior-driven development: Given-When-Then scenarios, shared language, executable specs (Cucumber/Gherkin). Use for behavior-focused specs.
pitfalls: Scenarios that test UI details, not behavior

name: e2e-testing
description: Write end-to-end tests (Playwright/Cypress/Selenium): critical user journeys, stability, flakiness control. Use for full-stack UI flows.

name: contract-testing
description: Verify service contracts (Pact/consumer-driven): prevent breaking API changes between producer and consumer. Use for service integrations.
checklist: Provider verified against contracts in CI
pitfalls: Integration breakage found only in prod

name: load-testing
description: Load/stress test systems (k6/Locust/JMeter/wrk): throughput, latency percentiles, breaking point. Use to validate performance/capacity.

name: property-testing
description: Write property-based tests (Hypothesis/fast-check/QuickCheck): invariants over generated inputs, shrinking. Use for logic with many edge cases.
pitfalls: Properties that are just the implementation

name: snapshot-testing
description: Use snapshot tests wisely: UI/output regression, reviewing diffs, avoiding rubber-stamping. Use for output-shape regression.
checklist: Snapshots small and reviewed on change
Not a substitute for behavior tests

name: fuzzing
description: Fuzz test to find crashes/security bugs (libFuzzer/AFL/go-fuzz/Atheris): coverage-guided random inputs. Use for parsers/untrusted input.

name: automation-scripting
description: Automate repetitive tasks with scripts (shell/Python/PowerShell): idempotency, error handling, logging, dry-run. Use to eliminate manual toil.
pitfalls: Fragile scripts with no error handling

name: web-scraping-legal
description: Scrape web data responsibly and legally: robots.txt, terms of service, rate limiting, public data only, no auth/paywall bypass. Use for permitted data collection.
checklist: Only public data; no CAPTCHA/auth bypass

name: browser-automation
description: Automate browsers (Playwright/Puppeteer/Selenium): navigation, forms, waits, headless, resilience. Use for UI automation of permitted sites.

name: data-format-conversion
description: Convert between data formats (JSON/YAML/TOML/XML/CSV/Parquet) losslessly with the right tools. Use for format conversion/interop.

name: file-format-handling
description: Read/write/validate structured file formats (JSON/YAML/TOML/XML/INI): schema validation, safe parsing. Use when handling config/data files.

name: csv-processing
description: Process CSV/TSV robustly: delimiters, quoting, encoding, large files, edge cases. Use for tabular text data.
pitfalls: Splitting on commas naively (breaks quoted fields)

name: pdf-processing
description: Extract, generate and manipulate PDFs (pdfplumber/pypdf/pdftotext): text/tables, merging, forms. Use for PDF tasks.
pitfalls: Assuming all PDFs have selectable text

name: image-processing
description: Process images (Pillow/ImageMagick/sharp): resize, convert, optimize, metadata, batch. Use for image manipulation.

name: text-processing
description: Process text at scale (grep/sed/awk/jq/Python): parsing, extraction, transformation, encoding. Use for text/log/data wrangling.
pitfalls: Regex where a real parser is needed

name: networking-fundamentals
description: Understand and debug networking: OSI layers, TCP/UDP, IP, DNS, NAT, ports, connectivity troubleshooting. Use for network issues.
checklist: DNS vs connectivity vs firewall isolated
pitfalls: Blaming the app for a DNS/firewall issue

name: http-protocol
description: Understand HTTP deeply: methods, status codes, headers, caching, cookies, HTTP/2-3, keep-alive. Use for HTTP-level debugging/design.

name: dns-management
description: Manage and debug DNS: record types, TTLs, propagation, resolvers, DNSSEC. Use for DNS setup/troubleshooting.

name: api-gateway
description: Design API gateways: routing, auth, rate limiting, transformation, aggregation. Use when fronting multiple services/APIs.
checklist: No business logic in the gateway
pitfalls: Gateway becoming a monolith of logic
Single point of failure without HA

name: make-interfaces-feel-better
description: Improve UI/UX quality: hierarchy, spacing, motion, feedback, empty/loading/error states, polish. Use when a UI feels rough.

name: design-systems
description: Build and use design systems: tokens, components, consistency, theming, documentation. Use for scalable, consistent UI.
pitfalls: One-off styles diverging from the system

name: ab-testing
description: Run valid A/B experiments: hypotheses, sample size, significance, guardrail metrics, avoiding peeking. Use for data-driven product decisions.
pitfalls: Stopping early on a lucky result (peeking)

name: i18n-l10n
description: Internationalize and localize apps: message catalogs, pluralization, dates/numbers, RTL, encoding. Use for multi-language products.

name: data-privacy
description: Handle personal data responsibly: minimization, consent, retention, anonymization, subject rights (GDPR/CCPA). Use when handling PII.
pitfalls: No deletion path for subject requests

name: opensource-publishing
description: Publish open-source responsibly: license, README, contributing, secret scrubbing, CI, releases. Use when open-sourcing a project.
checklist: No secrets in code or history

name: dart-language
description: Write, analyze and test Dart (Flutter and standalone): null safety, async, isolates. Use for .dart files and pubspec.yaml. Detect dart first.
